cases.reason: GR8 compares the connector's file-control attributes with the fixed file attributes and points at 9.1.6 for them. The 2002 9.1.6 list includes 'the padding character', which the 2002 file control entry can set with PADDING CHARACTER (12.3.4.10, an obsolete element in 2002). The 2023 9.1.6 list has no padding character, and the 2023 text has no PADDING CHARACTER clause at all. So in 2002 GR8 also covers a file whose entries specify PADDING CHARACTER, and the implementor must say whether OPEN validates it. The 2023 row (open_fixed_attribute_conflict, _ix) cannot show that case: the probe's program is refused at --std 2023 (COBOL0902). At --std 2002 the compiler accepts it with COBOL0903, and an OPEN INPUT through an entry with a different padding character returns '00'. That matches the documented implementor choice in docs/conformance/3.6 ('a fixed file attribute ... that OPEN does not validate'). That determination cites §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR8, not the 2002 rule.

cases.reason: GR11 decides which PERFORM sequences are undefined by the words 'within the range of that PERFORM statement'. It does not name the rule that defines that range, which is GR10. The 2002 GR10 range ends at an EXIT FUNCTION or EXIT METHOD transfer, and the 2023 GR1 range does not, because 2023 has neither statement (the reader marked GR10 DIFFERENT, removed-form). So in 2002, GR11's scope (an overlap is undefined, and no EC is set; outside the range a sequence is defined) reaches function and method source elements whose range boundary is EXIT FUNCTION or EXIT METHOD. The 2023 row has no test at all (a measured probe), and the reader's probe (perf-overlap-ec.cob) is a plain program. Class (d): a rule that defers to an unnamed rule that changed.
